source.label: The explicit formula for the Riesz mean from the real-part identity for xi'/xi alone, and the tilted reach in two strata

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: Notation of the Riesz mean explicit formula (R_L, D_L, F_L, X = e^L). Premise X: xi(s) = s(s-1) pi^(-s/2) Gamma(s/2) zeta(s)/2 is entire, its zeros are the nontrivial zeros rho with orders m_rho and real parts at most 1, and Re xi'/xi(s) = sum_rho m_rho (sigma - beta)/|s - rho|^2, absolutely convergent, wherever xi(s) is not 0. Under premise X alone: (0) xi'/xi(s) = C + sum_rho m_rho [1/(s - rho) - 1/(2 - rho)] and (zeta'/zeta)'(s) = 1/(s-1)^2 - sum_rho m_rho/(s - rho)^2 - sum_{q >= 1} 1/(s + 2q)^2; (1) for every L > 0 and every s other than 1, the rho and the points -2q, q >= 1: R_L(s) = -zeta'/zeta(s) + D_L(s-1) - sum_rho m_rho D_L(s-rho) - sum_{q >= 1} D_L(s+2q), the sums absolutely convergent; (2) for such s, Re R_L(s) = Re F_L(s-1) - sum_rho m_rho Re F_L(s-rho) + Re[psi(s/2 + 1)/2 - (log pi)/2] - sum_{q >= 1} Re D_L(s+2q).
claims.assessment: Conditional on one premise, with a complete elementary deduction: an entire function with constant real part is constant, which gives the partial fraction of xi'/xi and by differentiation that of (zeta'/zeta)' with absolutely convergent sums; for Re s > 1 the derivative in s of L R_L(s) is a Perron integral of (zeta'/zeta)' against X^w/w^2, which may be integrated term by term, each double pole giving the derivative of L F_L; the constant of integration vanishes as s tends to infinity, and the identity continues in s. Selberg's formula is not used. Premise X was read as a theorem statement in the density import's Lean project, which is not built here; the classical facts used beside it are the Dirichlet series of zeta'/zeta, the series of the digamma function and of its derivative.
claims.rationale: Removes the premise of the registered formula that had been read for one length only while its proof needed lengths tending to zero. The formula through which the tilted three-four-one statements are read now rests on one classical identity.
claims.next_action: None planned; a reading of premise X in a built proof or a textbook would make the lemma unconditional.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

claims.summary: Setting of the tilted local count reach (F, Phi, T_S, tilt a in (-1/2, 1/2), p = 1/2 - a). S0 a multiset, finite or not, of points with a < delta_rho <= delta0 < 1/2, c0 = delta0 - a, with at most kappa log(|t| + 3) points, with multiplicity, in |gamma_rho - t| <= 1 for every real t; S1 a finite multiset of points with a < delta_rho <= delta < 1/2, total multiplicity M, c = delta - a. If c0 L >= 2, |tau| >= 6p, (1/2 - delta) L >= log(12 M) + 2 log(p/c) and (1/2 - delta0) L >= log(kappa (174 + 66 log(|tau| + 4))) + 2 log(p/c0), then T_S(tau) >= 0 for S the union of S0 and S1. In particular, with S0 on the line (delta0 = 0, a < 0, |a| L >= 2): T_S(tau) >= 0 once (1/2 - delta) L >= log(12 M) + 2 log(p/c) and L/2 >= log(kappa (174 + 66 log(|tau| + 4))) + 2 log(p/|a|).
claims.assessment: Working proof in a few lines from the tilted local count reach and the tilted triangle positivity: the pole's term 2.25 Phi(p) is halved between the two strata, the first bounded by the local-count sum at its own distance c0 and the second by 8 M Phi(c). One instance at a negative tilt, 8001 points on the line and one pair, at a length the one-stratum condition does not cover, computed directly at four heights: T_S about 9.8e5 against a lower bound 6.9e5.
claims.rationale: For a configuration with all points on the line except finitely many, as the zeros of zeta with one hypothetical off-line zero, a sufficient condition for T_S >= 0 at a negative tilt with the same shape as the one on record for nonnegative tilts, 12 in place of 6, the points on the line costing a condition on the length, about 2 log log|tau| plus a term 4 log(p/|a|) in the tilt. A sufficient condition only: that the argument reaches exactly so far is not proved.
